seed_signals.title: European Commission Adopts First-Ever Strategy on Intergenerational Fairness
seed_signals.why_it_matters: This is the most significant institutional milestone for intergenerational fairness governance in the EU since the creation of the Commissioner portfolio itself. The strategy moves the concept from political rhetoric into the EU's legislative machinery — binding intergenerational fairness checks on all major proposals, annual monitoring, and a cross-cutting framework that spans competitiveness, social policy, climate, and territorial cohesion. No other major jurisdiction has institutionalised intergenerational fairness at this scale in the legislative process. The Council's subsequent preparation of conclusions (ST-8687/26) and the European Economic and Social Committee's opinion process signal multi-institutional embedding. For the platform's mission, this is a flagship signal of intergenerational equity becoming operational governance architecture.
seed_signals.growth_watch: Monitor corroboration, repeat sightings, and links to trend candidates for intergenerational-equity.

seed_signals.title: South Africa’s Constitutional Court Restores Order Invalidating Wild Coast Oil and Gas Exploration Rights
seed_signals.why_it_matters: The judgment operationalizes South Africa’s constitutional duty to protect the environment for present and future generations through concrete administrative-law remedies. It indicates that intergenerational environmental rights require lawful, precautionary and participatory decision-making before extractive rights are granted, rather than consultation after investments have been made. The refusal to remit a fatally flawed 13-year-old application also limits the ability of commercial actors to cure foundational rights violations retrospectively.
seed_signals.growth_watch: Monitor corroboration, repeat sightings, and links to trend candidates for climate-litigation.

seed_signals.title: South Korea National Assembly Amends Carbon Neutrality Act Post-Constitutional Court Intergenerational Ruling
seed_signals.why_it_matters: This represents East Asia's first successful constitutional climate case resulting in mandatory statutory revisions. It legally anchors post-2030 decarbonization obligations into South Korean primary law, preventing future parliaments from delaying industrial decarbonization at the expense of younger citizens.
seed_signals.growth_watch: Monitor corroboration, repeat sightings, and links to trend candidates for climate-litigation.

seed_signals.title: High Court of New Zealand Advances Full Trial in Landmark Customary Tort Case Smith v. Fonterra
seed_signals.why_it_matters: Smith v. Fonterra is globally unprecedented in combining indigenous customary law with common-law corporate tort liability. If the High Court recognizes a novel tort duty to cease emitting greenhouse gases that cause intergenerational cultural and material harm to coastal tribal lands, it will expose major corporate emitters worldwide to civil tort damages.
seed_signals.growth_watch: Monitor corroboration, repeat sightings, and links to trend candidates for climate-litigation.

seed_signals.title: New Zealand Government Introduces Legislation to Ban Climate Damage Lawsuits, Overriding Supreme Court Precedent
seed_signals.why_it_matters: New Zealand was previously a global leader in climate litigation, with its Supreme Court ruling in 2024 that a novel civil wrong of climate damage could be asserted in future proceedings. This legislative override represents one of the most aggressive pushbacks against climate litigation in any democracy, moving New Zealand from leader to outlier alongside the US. The case now has three concurrent legal fronts: the original Smith v Fonterra tort claim, Smith's High Court challenge to the Cabinet decision, and the bill's parliamentary passage. The Ombudsman's finding on withheld lobbyist documents adds a transparency dimension. The case tests whether executive power can retroactively extinguish common law rights recognized by the highest court, with implications for climate accountability frameworks worldwide.
seed_signals.growth_watch: Monitor corroboration, repeat sightings, and links to trend candidates for climate-litigation.

seed_signals.title: Ninth Circuit Dismisses Lighthiser v. Trump Youth Climate Challenge to Energy Executive Orders on Standing Grounds
seed_signals.why_it_matters: The ruling illustrates continuing judicial barriers youth plaintiffs face in federal court despite establishing overwhelming evidence of climate harm. The decision reinforces that separation-of-powers doctrines can block youth climate cases even when plaintiffs demonstrate concrete injuries, highlighting the gap between constitutional rights rhetoric and judicial remedies in US federal courts. The involvement of Held v. Montana veterans makes this a direct test of whether state-level climate precedent translates to federal forums.
seed_signals.growth_watch: Monitor corroboration, repeat sightings, and links to trend candidates for climate-litigation.

seed_signals.title: Borim Kim and Youth 4 Climate Action Win 2026 Goldman Environmental Prize for Landmark Korean Climate Litigation
seed_signals.why_it_matters: This is the first successful youth-led climate litigation in Asia, establishing that constitutional rights extend to future generations in an Asian legal system. The Goldman Prize recognition elevates the case as a global model for youth climate litigation outside Western legal systems. The Korean Constitutional Court's unanimous ruling that inadequate long-term climate targets violate future generations' rights creates a binding precedent for other Asian jurisdictions. For intergenerational equity, the case demonstrates that constitutional climate rights are enforceable across legal traditions, not only in common-law systems. Relationship memory: connects to the existing Korea Constitutional Court climate deadline signal (korea-constitutional-court-climate-deadline-2026-02-28) and the broader youth climate litigation arc (Held v. Montana, Netherlands Urgenda, Pakistan Lahore).

seed_signals.title: UK Treasury Committee: Student Loans System 'Mis-sold' to a Generation — MPs Say Government Has 'Moral Obligation' to Reverse Threshold Freeze
seed_signals.why_it_matters: This is one of the most direct parliamentary condemnations of intergenerational unfairness in education finance from any G7 legislature. The 'mis-sold' language is unusually strong for a committee report and the 'moral obligation' framing elevates the issue from policy disagreement to ethical duty. The 52,000 public responses demonstrate the scale of generational grievance. The report's finding that governments deliberately load costs onto younger generations hoping they 'will not notice' is a rare explicit acknowledgment of structural intergenerational exploitation in fiscal policy.
seed_signals.growth_watch: Monitor corroboration, repeat sightings, and links to trend candidates for intergenerational-fiscal-policy.

seed_signals.title: Australia Enacts Landmark Intergenerational Equity Tax Reform Limiting Negative Gearing and Restructuring CGT
seed_signals.why_it_matters: This is arguably the most concrete intergenerational equity fiscal reform enacted in any OECD country this year — now binding statute, not just a budget announcement. The mechanism shifts tax advantages away from established property investors (disproportionately older cohorts) toward new housing supply and younger buyers, making intergenerational equity an operational fiscal design principle. Australia is running parallel intergenerational equity arguments across tax, disability (NDIS Bill), national security, and biodiversity, making it a live laboratory for cross-domain translation.
seed_signals.growth_watch: Monitor corroboration, repeat sightings, and links to trend candidates for intergenerational-fiscal-policy.

seed_signals.title: South Korea Amends Constitutional Court Act to Allow Constitutional Complaints Against Final Court Judgments, Expanding Access to Rights Review
seed_signals.why_it_matters: This amendment fundamentally reshapes South Korea's constitutional architecture by making the Constitutional Court a final arbiter of constitutional rights even against judicial decisions. For intergenerational equity, the reform is significant because South Korea's Constitutional Court has been Asia's most active forum for future-generations rights claims - its August 2024 unanimous ruling in the youth climate case declared inadequate long-term climate targets a violation of future generations' constitutional rights. The new complaint mechanism means that future generations advocates can now challenge court decisions that fail to protect constitutional rights, including climate rights, creating a potential new pathway for enforcing intergenerational equity through the judiciary. The reform also creates a structural tension between the Supreme Court and Constitutional Court that will shape how constitutional rights - including future generations' rights - are adjudicated in Korea. Relationship memory: connects to the existing Korea Constitutional Court climate deadline signal (korea-constitutional-court-climate-deadline-2026-02-28) and the broader pattern of judicial architecture reforms affecting future-generations litigation.
seed_signals.growth_watch: Monitor corroboration, repeat sightings, and links to trend candidates for intergenerational-equity.

seed_signals.title: Hungary Misses Constitutional Court Deadline to Replace Climate Law Citing Intergenerational Justice
seed_signals.why_it_matters: Hungary is a rare case where intergenerational justice is constitutionally binding through the Climate Protection Act annulment — yet Parliament missed the court-ordered legislative deadline, testing whether future-generations protections can overcome electoral short-termism. The mechanism (constitutional omission finding plus delayed annulment of a static emissions cap) belongs to the same story arc as youth-backed climate litigation and the EU Intergenerational Fairness Strategy, but as a negative compliance comparator: statutory targets that age out can violate intergenerational equity if not continuously strengthened. Live gap: no replacement framework in force when the annulled provision expired.
seed_signals.growth_watch: Monitor corroboration, repeat sightings, and links to trend candidates for intergenerational-equity.

seed_signals.title: UN chief calls for a global AI child-safety pledge at the first Global Dialogue on AI Governance in Geneva
seed_signals.why_it_matters: This is the first time a UN Secretary-General has proposed a dedicated child-safety instrument inside the emerging multilateral AI-governance architecture, moving children's rights from a side concern to a headline demand. It gives youth and child-rights advocates a concrete, named commitment to hold governments and frontier labs to, and frames AI risk explicitly as a question of who is exposed now versus who is protected later.

seed_signals.title: European Commission Publishes First-Ever Strategy for Generational Renewal in Agriculture, Recommending 6% CAP Ring-Fence for Young Farmers
seed_signals.why_it_matters: This is the first time the European Commission has produced a dedicated strategy for generational renewal in agriculture, explicitly framing the demographic crisis in farming as an intergenerational fairness issue requiring structural intervention. The strategy's mechanisms - a Land Observatory, mandatory national strategies, integration into the European Semester - create institutional infrastructure for intergenerational governance in the agricultural sector, which accounts for a significant share of EU budget expenditure. The 6% vs 10% debate between the Commission and young farmers' organizations mirrors the broader tension between symbolic and structural intergenerational policy. The strategy's connection to the next CAP reform (post-2027) means it will shape how hundreds of billions in agricultural subsidies are distributed across generations. Relationship memory: connects to the EU Intergenerational Fairness Strategy signals and the broader pattern of EU institutions building intergenerational governance architecture across multiple policy domains.

seed_signals.title: Stimson Center Report: More Than Half of Pact for the Future Actions Show Progress, But UN Faces Existential Funding Crisis
seed_signals.why_it_matters: This is the first comprehensive, data-driven assessment of the Pact for the Future — the most ambitious UN reform agenda in a generation, which includes the Declaration on Future Generations as a core pillar. The finding that more than half of actions show progress is cautiously optimistic, but the ODA collapse and shrinking multilateral support create a stark headwind. For intergenerational equity advocates, the report provides the first systematic accountability mechanism for tracking whether the Declaration on Future Generations is being implemented, not just celebrated. The timing — UN Charter Day, with a new Secretary-General incoming — makes this a baseline assessment against which future progress will be measured.
seed_signals.growth_watch: Monitor corroboration, repeat sightings, and links to trend candidates for futures-governance.

seed_signals.title: UN Independent Scientific Panel's first AI assessment centres child harm and unequal Global South exposure
seed_signals.why_it_matters: This is the IPCC-style scientific baseline that future AI negotiations will cite, and its inaugural edition centres children and distributional, long-term harm rather than only frontier-model catastrophe. Embedding child safety, Global South exposure and language exclusion in the "minimum consensus" gives intergenerational-equity actors an authoritative, repeatedly-cited evidence anchor for who bears AI's costs over time.
seed_signals.growth_watch: Monitor corroboration, repeat sightings, and links to trend candidates for future-generations-governance.

seed_signals.title: Canadian Youth Sue Carney Government Over Climate Rollbacks, Testing Net-Zero Accountability Act
seed_signals.why_it_matters: This case is uniquely significant because it targets a leader — Mark Carney — who built his international reputation as a climate finance champion (Bank of England Governor, UN Special Envoy on Climate Action and Finance) but is now accused of gutting climate policy as Prime Minister. The irony is sharp: the man who warned markets about climate risk is now being sued by youth for failing to deliver a credible climate plan. The case also tests Canada's Net-Zero Emissions Accountability Act — one of the few laws globally that makes climate targets legally binding with a justiciable planning obligation. If the court orders the government to produce a compliant plan, it would establish a new model of climate accountability through statutory plan review rather than constitutional rights claims. The explicit contrast with European climate leadership frames Canada's rollbacks as both a legal violation and a strategic error in the emerging 'middle powers' democratic alliance.
seed_signals.growth_watch: Monitor corroboration, repeat sightings, and links to trend candidates for climate-litigation.

seed_signals.title: Environmental Groups File UN Human Rights Committee Complaint Challenging Australia's Fossil Fuel Exports as Human Rights Violations
seed_signals.why_it_matters: This complaint tests a critical frontier in climate litigation: whether states can be held accountable under international human rights law for emissions embedded in their fossil fuel exports. If the UNHRC finds the complaint admissible and rules against Australia, it would establish that fossil fuel exporting nations bear human rights obligations for downstream emissions - a principle with enormous implications for Australia (the world's third-largest fossil fuel exporter), the US, Canada, and other major exporters. The explicit reliance on the ICJ's 2025 advisory opinion creates a direct line from the ICJ's landmark ruling to individual human rights enforcement. For intergenerational equity, the complaint's framing of export emissions as intergenerational harm - current generations profiting from extraction while future generations bear climate costs - is a novel legal argument that could reshape the accountability landscape for fossil fuel trade.
seed_signals.growth_watch: Monitor corroboration, repeat sightings, and links to trend candidates for climate-litigation.

seed_signals.title: Montana's Held v. Montana Constitutional Climate Precedent Cited in International Litigation and UN Human Rights Fora
seed_signals.why_it_matters: Montana's constitutional climate precedent has become a globally cited reference point for the proposition that constitutional environmental rights are enforceable against government inaction on climate change. This is a direct international-commitments signal: a U.S. state court ruling is shaping the legal architecture of international climate obligations. The intergenerational mechanism is the 'forward-looking and preventative' interpretation - courts can act before harm is irreversible, protecting future generations who cannot vote or litigate today. The relationship memory connects to the ICJ climate advisory opinion, the IACtHR proceedings, and the wave of youth constitutional climate cases in South Korea, Germany, and Brazil. Montana's small-state constitutional innovation is having outsized international influence on the legal theory of intergenerational climate justice.
seed_signals.growth_watch: Monitor corroboration, repeat sightings, and links to trend candidates for youth-climate-governance.

seed_signals.title: EU Pact on Migration and Asylum Enters Full Application With Mandatory Child Safeguards — and Contested Detention of Children Aged 13+
seed_signals.why_it_matters: This is the single largest CHILD x MIGRATION regulatory shift in Europe this decade: it converts 'best interests of the child' from principle into operational obligations (guardianship, age assessment, schooling deadlines) binding on 27 member states simultaneously. The intergenerational fairness tension is explicit — the same package that codifies child safeguards also permits border-procedure detention of adolescents from 13, creating a two-tier treatment of children that will shape whether a generation of asylum-seeking minors is integrated or warehoused. It is a foresight anchor for tracking uneven national implementation, litigation risk, and the durability of child-rights guarantees under migration-restrictionist politics.

seed_signals.title: Madisonville, Texas City Council Establishes Inaugural Youth Council for High School Juniors and Seniors
seed_signals.why_it_matters: This is a municipal youth-seat instrument in a small Texas city: six 16–18-year-olds gain a standing advisory channel into the body that sets parks, streets, and budgets they will live with longer than sitting members. The intergenerational mechanism is a named Council-created youth council with bylaws, a fixed appointment vote, and a duty to put youth ideas on the adult agenda rather than one-off consultation.
seed_signals.growth_watch: Monitor corroboration, repeat sightings, and links to trend candidates for youth-governance.

seed_signals.title: Bangladesh Selected to Host Asia-Pacific Regional Conference of Youth 2026, Strengthening Youth Climate Diplomacy
seed_signals.why_it_matters: Bangladesh hosting RCOY Asia-Pacific 2026 is significant because it places one of the most climate-vulnerable countries at the centre of youth climate diplomacy. The RCOY mechanism is one of the few institutionalised channels through which youth voices formally feed into UNFCCC negotiations, making it a concrete governance structure rather than a symbolic platform. The 12-organisation, 10-country coalition demonstrates the growing institutionalisation of youth climate organising in the Asia-Pacific region. For the platform's youth governance dimension, this signal shows how youth climate participation is moving from protest-based advocacy to structured diplomatic engagement with formal outputs (National Youth Statements, Regional Youth Statement, Global Youth Statement) that enter the COP negotiation process.
seed_signals.growth_watch: Monitor corroboration, repeat sightings, and links to trend candidates for youth-climate-governance.

seed_signals.title: Planning (Wales) Act 2026 Hardwires the Future Generations Sustainable-Development Duty Across the Planning Code
seed_signals.why_it_matters: This makes the future-generations principle the operative test for how Wales plans its built environment, not just an aspirational goal — the clearest example globally of a jurisdiction fusing statutory long-term wellbeing duties with the day-to-day machinery of urban and regional planning. The mechanism is legal: every tier of spatial planning, from the national framework to local development plans, must be exercised through the sustainable-development lens of the 2015 Act, giving the interests of future residents a durable foothold in decisions with multi-decade consequences. It matters as a transferable model as the EU (via the Intergenerational Fairness Strategy's 'fair places' pillar) and other governments look for concrete ways to operationalise future-generations commitments in cities. Relationship memory: complements the Wales Future Generations Commissioner signals and the Environment (Wales) Act 2026 already tracked here, and contrasts with Scotland's January 2026 rejection of a Wellbeing and Sustainable Development Bill — underscoring that the Welsh model of embedding future generations in law remains distinctive even within the UK.
seed_signals.growth_watch: Monitor corroboration, repeat sightings, and links to trend candidates for future-generations-governance.

seed_signals.title: ILO Adopts First-Ever Binding Convention on Decent Work in the Platform Economy
seed_signals.why_it_matters: This is a landmark structural shift: for the first time, international law formally recognises gig workers' labour rights as a global governance concern, not a domestic classification dispute. The convention creates a ratification pathway and implementation pressure for ILO's 190+ member states — a governance mechanism that could reshape how hundreds of millions of platform workers worldwide, disproportionately young people, are treated by platform firms. The explicit algorithmic management provisions bring AI governance directly into labour law, connecting digital governance and youth labour rights in a single binding instrument.
seed_signals.growth_watch: Monitor corroboration, repeat sightings, and links to trend candidates for jobs-labor-rights.

seed_signals.title: UN Secretary-General Guterres Delivers Major Climate Address at London Climate Action Week: "A Tale of Two Crises"
seed_signals.why_it_matters: This address is significant for intergenerational governance on multiple levels. First, Guterres explicitly framed the climate crisis as an intergenerational justice issue — "those who did the least to cause these crises pay the highest price." Second, the seven-point plan includes concrete demands for AI transparency and renewable-powered data centres, connecting digital governance to climate justice. Third, the tipping points report from the UN Scientific Advisory Board provides the scientific foundation for why delayed action constitutes intergenerational harm. The address also came just days after the US Ninth Circuit dismissed the Lighthiser youth climate case, creating a stark contrast between international and domestic legal responses to climate intergenerational equity. The call to tax fossil fuel profits to support vulnerable communities directly addresses the intergenerational transfer of climate costs.
seed_signals.growth_watch: Monitor corroboration, repeat sightings, and links to trend candidates for climate-governance.

seed_signals.title: ILO, Nigeria and France Launch Phase 2 of Just Transition Project to Create Green Jobs and Integrate Climate Action with Employment
seed_signals.why_it_matters: Nigeria is Africa's largest economy and a major fossil fuel producer, making its just transition pathway globally significant for intergenerational equity. The explicit integration of just transition principles into NDC 3.0 creates a binding framework for ensuring that climate action does not disproportionately harm young and vulnerable workers. With one of the world's youngest populations (median age ~18), Nigeria's transition from fossil fuels to green jobs is a defining intergenerational challenge: today's policy choices determine whether the youth bulge becomes a demographic dividend or a crisis.
seed_signals.growth_watch: Monitor corroboration, repeat sightings, and links to trend candidates for climate-justice.

action_window.label: Formal Council adoption of EU Intergenerational Fairness conclusions

act_now.why_now: Present-horizon signal with immediate policy relevance.
act_now.rationale: The Netherlands is moving from ad hoc generational analysis toward institutionalising intergenerational fiscal scrutiny at the heart of budget-making — a pathway distinct from Wales' wellbeing-goals legislation or Italy's regulatory impact assessment. Senate adoption creates political pressure on the executive to embed generational testing in the Miljoenennota even though implementation status remains 'not executed.' Combined with the EU's new Intergenerational Fairness Strategy citing the Dutch generatietoets as a member-state model, this positions the Netherlands as a fiscal-governance test case for operationalising intergenerational equity without a dedicated future-generations commissioner.

act_now.rationale: Boletín 16.441-19 represents Latin America's most advanced statutory effort to institutionalize national strategic foresight and intergenerational planning into permanent law. The parliamentary tensions reflect the classic governance trade-offs of anticipatory institutions: establishing an agency independent enough to challenge short-term electoral cycles while resolving executive-legislative appointment vetoes, ensuring real bureaucratic authority over ministerial budget lines, and avoiding downgrade into an underfunded advisory council.

act_now.title: Ofcom Issues Record Online Safety Act Fines for Failed Child Age-Assurance, Led by £1.35m Penalty on 8579 LLC

action_window.label: Budget-cycle check on intergenerational fairness tests

act_now.why_now: Present-horizon signal with immediate policy relevance.
act_now.rationale: This is implementation evidence for the UK’s child-online-safety legal architecture, not a new ban. The mechanism is regulator-driven age assurance and geoblocking that removes specific high-harm services from children’s information environment now, while preserving existing OSA duties so the announced under-16 social-media ban cannot be treated as a pause or clawback. Who benefits now: children currently exposed to suicide, self-harm and graphic-violence sites. The open letter is a counter-to-the-counter: it blocks a possible industry reading that future primary legislation displaces present child-safety duties. Civic-access costs remain a live intergenerational tension because geoblocking and forthcoming age-16 checks can also shrink lawful information spaces for older minors.

act_now.title: Montana Held v. Montana Precedent Cited in New Zealand Climate Litigation Ban Debate as Counterexample of Constitutional Climate Rights

action_window.label: Budget-cycle check on intergenerational fairness tests

act_now.why_now: Transition-horizon signal likely to shape near-term institutional choices.
act_now.rationale: This signal fills the international-commitments gap by documenting how Montana constitutional climate precedent is being invoked in a global debate about legislative backlash against climate litigation. New Zealand proposed ban on climate tort claims represents a direct legislative response to the success of climate litigation — and Held v. Montana is cited as the proof-of-concept that constitutional climate rights are enforceable. The intergenerational equity dimension is sharp: New Zealand government is using retrospective legislation to extinguish an existing climate lawsuit brought by an indigenous activist (Mike Smith, a MÄori elder), while Montana precedent shows constitutional rights can withstand legislative attempts to shield fossil fuel interests. The debate creates a live comparison between two common-law jurisdictions on whether courts or legislatures should determine climate obligations to future generations. Relationship memory: connects to the ICJ advisory opinion citation of Held, the UN Special Rapporteur references, and the broader global pattern of legislative backlash against climate litigation (Montana SB 97 venue law, New Zealand Climate Change Response Act amendment).

act_now.title: New Zealand MSD Publishes Official Child Impact Assessment Tool for Laws and Policies

action_window.label: Budget-cycle check on intergenerational fairness tests

act_now.why_now: Transition-horizon signal likely to shape near-term institutional choices.
act_now.rationale: This is the official New Zealand child-IA methodology — the closest cousin to a CRWIA — and it is missing from the foresight corpus. Mechanism: agencies are expected to apply Children's Convention principles and may use the CIA templates before adopting a law or policy, but there is no statutory requirement to complete a CIA as a precondition for Cabinet or Budget decisions. Mana Mokopuna's February 2026 Budget Policy Statement submission urged mandatory use of this government-endorsed tool for Budget 2026, confirming the instrument still exists and is not being used as a binding gate.

act_now.title: NOAA Advances First U.S. Commercial Deep-Seabed Recovery Application Despite Unresolved International Governance Conflict

action_window.label: Budget-cycle check on intergenerational fairness tests

act_now.why_now: Transition-horizon signal likely to shape near-term institutional choices.
act_now.rationale: This is the first U.S. commercial-recovery application to advance through a national pathway for seabed beyond national jurisdiction. It could accelerate extraction decisions affecting slow-forming ecosystems and resources characterized internationally as the common heritage of humankind before a multilateral Mining Code is agreed. The event exposes a long-horizon governance fracture over whether irreversible environmental risk and benefits owed to future generations are governed collectively or through unilateral national authorization.

act_now.title: New Zealand Passes Parental-Income Test Cutting Jobseeker Support for Most 18- and 19-Year-Olds

action_window.label: Budget-cycle check on intergenerational fairness tests

act_now.why_now: Present-horizon signal with immediate policy relevance.
act_now.rationale: This is a youth-opportunity rollback using a fiscal-sustainability frame. The mechanism is a parental-means test that shifts income support for unemployed 18- and 19-year-olds from the public budget onto family balance sheets from November 2026. Who benefits now: current taxpayers and older homeowners exempted from the tighter Accommodation Supplement test (superannuitants, veterans and supported-living recipients are carved out). Who pays: young people whose parents earn above the threshold, including many with mental-health conditions who cannot immediately work, and later cohorts if early benefit exclusion raises long-run NEET scarring. The housing change is an intergenerational incidence twist: working-age homeowner subsidies tighten while pensioner homeowners are protected.
